findings.plain_summary: OPM matched Treasury's August 2026 Death Record Confidence Scoring Tool against FEHB enrollment records and found about 50,000 deceased people still listed, with $96.3 million in improper payments after date of death plus an estimated $10.4 million in carrier costs. OPM says it will next review claims that may have been paid after date of death, and the Director called these findings a 'drop in the bucket' of what the integrity program expects to find.

items.headline: About 50,000 deceased individuals found still enrolled in FEHB
items.what_changes: OPM matched Treasury's August 2026 DRCST death data against FEHB enrollment records and found about 50,000 deceased people still listed in the program.
items.speaker: OPM
items.quote: The US Office of Personnel Management (OPM) has identified approximately 50,000 deceased individuals who remain listed in the Federal Employees Health Benefits Program (FEHBP) by matching Treasury’s August 2026 Death Record Confidence Scoring Tool (DRCST) against OPM’s FEHB enrollment records.

items.headline: $96.3M paid after death: $70.6M in premium contributions, $25.7M in retirement payments
items.what_changes: The review found $96.3 million in improper post-death payments. This includes $70.6 million in government FEHB premium contributions and $25.7 million in retirement (annuity) payments.
items.speaker: OPM
items.quote: including $70.6 million in government FEHB premium contributions and $25.7 million in retirement payments.

items.headline: OPM will next review medical claims paid after date of death
items.what_changes: OPM plans a further review in the coming weeks of claims that may have been paid after enrollees died. This is a cost category not included in the $106.7 million total.
items.speaker: OPM
items.quote: OPM will examine claims that may have been paid after date of death in the coming weeks.

items.headline: $10.4M estimated carrier costs for 20,000+ people kept on carrier rolls without government premium
items.what_changes: More than 20,000 individuals remain on carrier rolls with no government premium being paid for them. Carriers still charge FEHB funds monthly for administrative and per-member costs, an estimated $10.4 million.
items.speaker: OPM
items.quote: tied to over 20,000 individuals who remain on carrier rolls even though no government premium is being paid for them.

items.headline: OPM Director signals findings are a fraction of what integrity program expects to find
items.what_changes: Director Kupor characterized the $106.7 million as a 'drop in the bucket.' This signals expanded integrity reviews and larger expected findings ahead.
items.speaker: OPM
items.quote: These findings are a drop in the bucket of what we expect to find as we double down on our integrity program

could_not_determine: The time period over which the $96.3 million in post-death payments accrued.
How or whether OPM will recover the improper payments, and from whom (estates, survivors, carriers).
Whether or when the roughly 50,000 records will be removed, and whether survivor annuitants or family members on self-and-family enrollments could be affected.
The accuracy or false-positive rate of the DRCST match, and whether matches will be verified before action.
The dollar amount of medical claims paid after date of death; OPM has not yet reviewed these.
Which carriers hold the 20,000+ records with no government premium.
Whether any changes to FEHB procedures, regulations, or carrier contracts will follow.

findings.plain_summary: OPM announced that applications are open for the 2027–2028 class of the White House Fellows Program, a full-time, paid, one-year fellowship in Washington, DC, where Fellows work with cabinet secretaries and senior officials. The release describes the program's history (nearly 900 alumni since 1964) but gives no deadline, eligibility criteria, or class size.

items.headline: Applications open now for 2027–2028 class; no deadline stated
items.what_changes: OPM opened applications for the 2027–2028 White House Fellows class. The release gives no closing date, eligibility rules, or number of slots, and refers readers to an external link instead.
items.speaker: OPM
items.quote: Applications for the 2027–2028 White House Fellows class are open now.

items.headline: Fellowship is full-time, paid, and based in Washington, DC
items.what_changes: Selected Fellows serve a full-time, paid year in DC working directly with senior administration officials. They also take part in an education program and community service activities. The pay level is not specified.
items.speaker: OPM
items.quote: Selected Fellows participate in a full-time, paid fellowship in Washington, DC, where they work directly with senior administration officials on consequential issues facing the nation.

items.headline: Program has had nearly 900 participants since 1964
items.what_changes: This is the only scale figure in the release: nearly 900 total alumni since the program was founded. That implies small annual classes.
items.speaker: OPM
items.quote: Since its founding, nearly 900 Americans have participated in the program, including Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff Dan Caine, former Secretary of State General Colin Powell, former Secretary of Transportation Elaine Chao, Pulitzer Prize-winning historian Doris Kearns Goodwin, and US Senators Bill Hagerty and Dan Sullivan.

could_not_determine: Application deadline or closing date
Eligibility requirements (citizenship, education, career stage, federal employee eligibility)
Number of Fellows to be selected for the 2027–2028 class
Salary or compensation level and pay authority for Fellows
Fellowship start and end dates
Selection process and timeline, including the role of the President's Commission on White House Fellows
Whether any changes were made to the program structure compared with prior years
The application link URL (rendered only as 'here' in the text)

findings.plain_summary: Under the President's alternative pay plan, GS base pay and locality rates stay at 2026 levels in 2027, but OPM will use special salary rate authority to raise pay 3.8% for about 140,000 law enforcement employees already on Special Rate Tables L001–L140, effective January 10, 2027. OPM will also automatically extend these special rates to more law enforcement categories, giving them about a 6.7% increase, unless an agency opts out by November 25, 2026.

items.headline: GS base pay and locality pay frozen at 2026 levels for 2027
items.what_changes: Under the President's alternative plan, GS and other statutory base pay rates and locality percentages stay at 2026 levels in January 2027. Only targeted special-rate increases are provided.
items.speaker: OPM
items.quote: Under the alternative plan, General Schedule (GS) and other base pay rates for statutory pay systems will remain at 2026 levels, as will locality pay percentages.

items.headline: 3.8% raise for about 140,000 employees on Special Rate Tables L001–L140, effective January 10, 2027
items.what_changes: All existing law enforcement special rate tables L001–L140 rise 3.8%. They currently cover about 140,000 employees. The increase takes effect the first pay period on or after January 1, 2027 (January 10, 2027).
items.speaker: OPM
items.quote: Increase current Special Rate Tables L001 through L140 by 3.8 percent in January 2027. These special rate tables were established to provide a 3.8-percent increase in January 2026 for around 140,000 employees in certain law enforcement positions.

items.headline: Newly covered law enforcement personnel get about 6.7%, not 3.8%
items.what_changes: Newly covered employees receive the 2.77% catch-up increase that current table employees got in 2026, compounded with the 3.8% (1.038 × 1.0277 – 1 = 6.68%). This brings them to common pay levels, subject to statutory caps.
items.speaker: OPM
items.quote: Agencies should note that these changes in coverage will result in newly covered law enforcement personnel receiving increases of approximately 6.7 percent over their current pay, subject to applicable statutory pay caps.

items.headline: Expanded coverage is automatic unless the agency opts out by November 25, 2026
items.what_changes: New special rate coverage applies by default. To opt out, an agency must send a letter from the agency head or a designee (e.g., CHCO or HR Director) to PayPolicy@opm.gov by November 25, 2026. The same deadline applies to opt-outs for non-GS positions and to questions or comments.
items.speaker: OPM
items.quote: Such new special rate coverage will apply automatically unless an agency sends OPM a request to be excluded from such coverage, following the instructions provided below and in the attachment.

items.headline: Four new GS categories added; LEOs covered only through detainee contact are excluded
items.speaker: OPM
items.quote: GS employees serving in approved LEO positions (as defined in 5 U.S.C. 5541(3)), excluding employees who are covered by section 5541(3) based on frequent direct contact with detained suspected/convicted criminals (see 5 U.S.C. 8401(17)(D));
items.section: New Special Rate Coverage for Additional GS Law Enforcement Positions

items.headline: VA police on title 38 special rates excluded and handled separately
items.what_changes: Department of Veterans Affairs police officers covered by title 38 special rates are left out of the GS-0083 expansion. Their January 2027 adjustment will be handled separately.
items.speaker: OPM
items.quote: GS employees serving in the 0083 Police occupational series, excluding police officers in the Department of Veterans Affairs who are covered by title 38 special rates and whose January 2027 pay adjustment will be handled separately;
items.section: New Special Rate Coverage for Additional GS Law Enforcement Positions

items.headline: Pay caps may reduce or eliminate increases for some employees
items.what_changes:
Two statutory limits apply:
- Special rates cannot exceed Executive Schedule level IV, which stays at $197,200 in 2027.
- A grade's special rate minimum cannot be more than 30% above that grade's maximum base rate.
Employees near these limits may get less than 3.8% or 6.7%, or nothing.
items.speaker: OPM
items.quote: Therefore, employees at or near these limits in 2026 may see no increase in their pay or receive increases of less than 3.8 percent for currently covered employees or of less than 6.7 percent for newly covered employees in January 2027.

items.headline: Non-GS law enforcement positions also covered, including new 6.68% coverage
items.what_changes: Positions continuing from 2026 get 3.8%: Secret Service Uniformed Division, Diplomatic Security agents and investigators, Park Police, and NNSA nuclear materials couriers. Newly covered positions get 6.68%: Commerce and Peace Corps FP-1811 investigators, and SEC non-supervisory SK-1811 investigators (subject to consultation with OPM). All are capped at EX-IV.
items.speaker: OPM
items.quote: OPM plans to authorize the following agencies to implement special salary rates under 5 U.S.C. 5305 and 5 CFR 530, subpart C, to provide a 6.68-percent total increase for the following positions, which were not authorized to receive a 3.8-percent total increase for the January 2026 pay adjustment:

items.headline: OPM considering 3.8% special rates for CBP agricultural inspectors and certain firefighters
items.what_changes: These protective, non-law-enforcement positions may get special rates. This is separate from the President's directive and depends on staffing data showing recruitment or retention problems. OPM staff will contact the affected agencies by email.
items.speaker: OPM
items.quote: Separately from implementing special rates in January 2027 following the President’s alternative plan, OPM is considering whether to establish special rates to provide a 3.8- percent increase in January 2027 for U.S. Customs and Border Protection agricultural inspectors and for certain firefighters.

items.headline: Coverage expansion is prospective only, with no retroactive 2026 catch-up
items.what_changes: Newly covered employees receive no back pay for the 2.77% special rate increase they did not get in 2026. Their pay levels are equalized only going forward.
items.speaker: OPM
items.quote: Note that these coverage changes will be prospective and not retroactive.

could_not_determine: How many employees will be newly covered by the expanded special rate coverage (GS or non-GS)
Estimated cost of the 3.8% and 6.7% increases
Which specific Office of Inspector General positions and 'others' will be newly covered
How the January 2027 pay adjustment for VA title 38 police officers will be handled
Whether OPM will in fact establish special rates for CBP agricultural inspectors and firefighters, and how many employees that would cover
How many employees are at or near the Executive Schedule level IV cap or the 30-percent statutory limit and would get reduced or no increases
What criteria, if any, OPM will use to evaluate agency opt-out requests

stories.headline: 2027 GS pay frozen; law enforcement special rates rise 3.8% to 6.7%
stories.takeaway: GS base and locality pay stay at 2026 levels in 2027, while about 140,000 employees on law enforcement special rate tables L001–L140 get 3.8% effective January 10, 2027. Newly covered law enforcement categories get about 6.7% automatically unless their agency opts out by November 25, 2026.

stories.takeaway: A match against Treasury death data found about 50,000 deceased individuals still listed in FEHB, with $96.3 million paid after death ($70.6 million in government premium contributions and $25.7 million in retirement payments) plus an estimated $10.4 million in carrier costs. OPM will next review medical claims paid after date of death, a cost category not included in these totals.
